Flex creates a scanner from rules for words, numbers, and symbols. Bison creates a parser from grammar rules. Together, they support Lex/Yacc experiments, but students usually manage the files and run several compilation commands themselves.

Compiler Explorer lets users compile code in a browser and inspect the generated compiler output. It provides a useful example of presenting the source code and compilation results together in one interface.

The ANTLRWorks research describes a grammar editor with an interpreter and a visual debugger. These features help users inspect parsing behavior, investigate grammar errors, and understand how the grammar handles a given input.
Sources: Flex and Bison manuals, Compiler Explorer documentation, ANTLRWorks research.

Flex manual: https://westes.github.io/flex/manual/Introduction.html
GNU Bison manual: https://www.gnu.org/s/bison/manual/bison.html
Compiler Explorer official documentation: https://github.com/compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer/blob/main/docs/WhatIsCompilerExplorer.md
Bovet, J. and Parr, T. (2008). ANTLRWorks: an ANTLR grammar development environment. Software: Practice and Experience, 38(12), 1305-1332. https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.872

The reviewed tools address different parts of compiler learning. Flex and Bison generate working scanners and parsers, Compiler Explorer provides browser-based experimentation, and ANTLRWorks explains grammar behavior through visual tools.

Lexora brings these approaches into a dedicated workspace for Lex/Yacc laboratory practice. Students can edit specifications, run them using Flex, Bison, and GCC, and examine syntax trees, symbols, and intermediate code for supported input.

Lexora's contribution is the connection between execution and learning views. Its built-in analyzer runs separately from the submitted Lex/Yacc grammar, so the visual results describe Lexora's supported input language.

Flex manual: https://westes.github.io/flex/manual/Introduction.html
GNU Bison manual: https://www.gnu.org/s/bison/manual/bison.html
Compiler Explorer official documentation: https://github.com/compiler-explorer/compiler-explorer/blob/main/docs/WhatIsCompilerExplorer.md
Bovet, J. and Parr, T. (2008). ANTLRWorks: an ANTLR grammar development environment. Software: Practice and Experience, 38(12), 1305-1332. https://doi.org/10.1002/spe.872
The relationship between the reviewed approaches and Lexora is a design synthesis. Lexora-specific claims derive from backend/services/compiler.js and backend/services/inputAnalysis.js. The project does not claim that no related website exists, or that it traces every submitted grammar.
